ov: Fish that hatch in rivers, go to sea to grow, then return to fresh water to spawn, usually in the stream where they hatched. The Atlantic salmon lives in the North Atlantic, and six Pacific species in the North Pacific.

why.dm: Wild salmon aren’t domesticated, but salmon are intensively farmed. Norway is the largest producer, followed by Chile.
why.et: An important food fish, farmed heavily; Norway is the biggest producer, then Chile.

rg: Rivers and seas of the North Atlantic and North Pacific; introduced to the Great Lakes, Patagonia and New Zealand.
fx: Pacific and Atlantic salmon split 10 to 20 million years ago, long before the ice ages.

_cf.tip: Trout and salmon are close relatives in the same family, with similar migrations; most trout stay in fresh water.
